Hi Claire — thanks for the sheet, I filled section A and attached a one-page export (kimberly_hostedapi_answers_tabbed.pdf) for procurement. High-level answers below; the PDF has a row-by-row mapping to your spreadsheet.

Quick summary (hosted API default behavior):

- Physical storage: Requests are processed in the customer-requested region where available (we route to the nearest supported region). Persistent storage of raw request/response content does not occur by default for hosted API calls — transient copies exist in memory and ephemeral cache during processing.

- Logs & audit trails: Minimal audit logs (timestamps, routing decisions, request/response metadata without PII by default) are stored for troubleshooting and billing. Audit logs are stored in encrypted object storage in the same region as the processing cluster.

- Default retention windows (out-of-the-box):
  • Raw request/response store: 0 days (not persisted) unless customer opts into "retention for support" during onboarding.
  • Troubleshooting retention (opt-in): up to 30 days by default; can be contractually capped to 7/14/30 days.
  • KV/prefix cache (in-memory + short-lived local disk spill): ephemeral, TTL typically 30 minutes; not included in backups.
  • Audit logs (operational + billing): 90 days by default; can be shortened to 30 days in enterprise policy addendum.
  • Aggregated metrics and usage summaries: retained for 13 months for billing and product analytics (can be masked/rolled up to remove identifiers).

- Backups & snapshots: System-level backups (metadata and control-plane state) are encrypted and retained for 90 days for disaster recovery. Customer-requested data retention for support does not get copied into long-term cross-region backups unless explicitly authorized.

- Deletion / erase process:
  • If a customer requests a data purge, we open a secure erase ticket with our infra team. For opt-in retained data we target a 72-hour SLA to remove primary copies and 7 days to remove any short-lived replicas or cached artifacts.
  • For backups/snapshots, deletion is initiated and those objects are retired and made unrecoverable within our backup retention window; we provide a deletion certificate once purge completes.

- Evidence & audit: We can provide a deletion certificate and a log of erase actions (redacted where necessary) and a signed statement of compliance for the purged objects. SOC 2 and contractual audit attachments are available on request.

Options to tighten controls at contracting:
 1) Region-locking addendum (guarantee processing and storage in X region only).
 2) Shortened audit log retention (30-day maximum).
 3) Opt-out of any troubleshooting retention and restrict all request/response persistence to 0 days.
 4) Require customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key, BYOK) for stored artifacts and backups.

See answers tab in the PDF and the linked Drive folder for architecture notes. If helpful, Aditya can add a short technical appendix about backup lifecycle and key management.

Regards,

Adding a few technical clarifications to Kim's high-level answers:

- Transient processing: For hosted API requests we keep tokenization buffers and KV caches in RAM and ephemeral SSDs attached to the serving node; these are zeroed on instance termination. They are not written to long-term object storage unless the customer enables debugging/troubleshooting retention.

- Opt-in retention mechanics: When a customer enables "troubleshooting retention" we store encrypted request/response payloads in object storage for the agreed period. These objects are labeled with an internal retention TTL and are automatically garbage-collected by our retention controller at expiry.

- Encryption & keys: All at-rest storage uses AES-256. By default we manage keys; with BYOK the encrypted blobs are wrapped with the customer's KEK stored in the customer's KMS (supported providers: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).

- Backups & immutable snapshots: Backups use incremental snapshots. When a delete request is issued for an object that appears in an incremental snapshot, we mark that object as deleted in the snapshot index and ensure it is not restored for restoration operations after retention controller completes its cycle. Complete physical shredding from backup media occurs within the backup retention expiry (up to 90 days unless otherwise contracted).

- Audit trail for deletion: Delete operations generate a signed event in our internal audit ledger (hash chained). We can export events scoped to the customer's tenant for the window requested (redacting operator identities where required).

Happy to jump on a short call if your procurement or engineering teams want to walk through the appendix.
